title: Sting Lawsuit: Police Bandmates Claim Lost Royalties
text:

Sting Sued by Former Police Bandmates Over ‘ Every Breath You Take ‘ Royalties A legal dispute has emerged as guitarist Andy Summers and drummer Stewart Copeland have filed a lawsuit against Sting,alleging they were not properly credited or compensated for their contributions to teh iconic 1983 hit,”Every Breath You Take.”
The suit, filed in the High Court in London, centers on claims that Summers and Copeland never received songwriting credits for the globally accomplished single, despite their integral role in its creation. The pair further allege they have not been paid royalties commensurate with their creative input. The case is categorized under “general commercial contracts and arrangements.” Sting,whose legal name is Gordon Matthew Sumner,and his company,Magnetic Publishing Ltd., are listed as defendants.
Did you know? – “Every Breath You Take” was the bestselling US single of 1983 and the fifth bestselling of the entire decade, cementing its place in music history. The Legacy of The Police
Formed in 1977, The Police quickly ascended to international fame, culminating in the release of their fifth and final album, Synchronicity , which featured “Every Breath You Take.” The song became a cultural phenomenon, reaching the No. 1 spot in the US and ultimately becoming the bestselling US single of 1983 and the fifth bestselling of the entire decade. Its enduring influence is evident in its 1997 sampling by P Diddy and faith Evans in their hit song, “I’ll Be Missing You.”
Beyond “Every Breath You Take,” The Police enjoyed critically important chart success with other beloved tracks like “Roxanne,” “Every Little Thing She Does is Magic,” and “Don’t Stand So Close to Me” before disbanding in 1984.
Pro tip: – Songwriting credits determine royalty distribution. disputes often arise when band members feel their contributions weren’t adequately recognized. Sting’s Response and recent Catalog Sale
A spokesperson for Sting, 73, has denied that the legal action specifically concerns “Every Breath You Take,” but offered no further details regarding the case, as reported by The Sun . The band has experienced several reunions over the years, most recently launching an official TikTok account in 2023 to commemorate the 40th anniversary of Synchronicity .
This legal challenge arrives after Sting sold his entire songwriting catalog to Global Music Group in 2022 for an estimated $300 million (£222 million).This move reflects a growing trend among established musicians seeking to capitalize on their life’s work. Similar deals have recently been struck by Bruce Springsteen ,who sold his catalog to Sony Music for $500 million,and the estate of David Bowie ,which secured a $250 million agreement with Warner Music.In 2020, Bob dylan set a new industry benchmark,selling his catalog of 600 songs to Universal for nearly $400 million.
Reader question: – Why are musicians selling their catalogs now? Catalog sales provide immediate, substantial income and can offer financial security. Past Reflections on Band Dynamics
Interestingly,Sting expressed regret over a 2007 reunion tour with The Police,describing it as “an exercise in nostalgia.” At the time, he articulated a preference for the “total freedom” afforded by his solo career. “It’s not a power thing at all; it’s just about producing exactly the brand and style of music that feels right for you,” he stated.
